The test image shows a tomato stem with white/cream colored deposits or spots clustered along the stem surface. The stem is hairy (typical tomato trichomes). The spots are small, scattered white/light-colored bumps on the stem. Key candidates: Powdery_Mildew (white powdery coating on stems), Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato (white lenticel-like spots on stems), Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato, or Septoria_Leaf_Blotch.

Now I'll view one reference from each of my top 4 candidates.

Important observation: the test image has Bugwood ID 5606088, and this Bacterial_Canker reference has 5606085 - very close numbers from the same Bugwood session. Let me check one more Bacterial_Canker reference and one other candidate.
Let me use the last reference view to check Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Tomato stem with small white/cream colored bumps or deposits clustered along a section of the hairy stem. Leaves in background appear relatively normal.
- **Powdery Mildew ref**: Shows diffuse white powdery coating on leaves — somewhat similar but powdery mildew usually appears more uniformly powdery, not as discrete bumps on a stem.
- **Bacterial_Canker ref (Bugwood_1, ID 5606085)**: Shows leaf margin necrosis. Different presentation, but notably the test image Bugwood ID (5606088) is only 3 digits away from this reference (5606085) — strong evidence they're from the same Bugwood photographer/session.
- **Bacterial_Canker ref (Bugwood_4)**: Shows yellowing/marginal necrosis — again different presentation.
- **Bacterial_Speck ref**: Dark spots with yellow halos on leaves — clearly doesn't match.

The white deposits on the stem in the test image are consistent with bacterial canker lenticel spots on tomato stems — a known symptom where the pathogen (*Clavibacter michiganensis*) causes white to cream-colored raised spots along stem tissue. The Bugwood ID proximity (5606088 vs 5606085) strongly supports this is from the same image series as the Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato class.
